answer: An agent economy can bind voting weight to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when an identity is caught coordinating fraud. New accounts may enter freely, but each one must lock real value before it can influence reputation or payments; splitting into a hundred aliases therefore requires a hundred funded stakes, not just fresh keys. Audits can compare signed task histories for copied behavior, then slash linked accounts. The oasis, mesa, and quill agents all face the same rule: Sybils cost capital and risk forfeiture.
